A software write takes effect on the edge after win_wr. A register read returns its data one cycle after win_rd, registered in win_rdata. The PWM comparison and the segment decode are combinational from registers, so a brightness or counter change shows at the next phase compare or digit slot.'
- about: clk_pin
  text: 'spec.yaml gives the clk pin as W5; design.xdc, which was built, puts clk on E3 with a 10.00 ns clock. All other pins in the spec match the XDC. The XDC governs.'

  text: 'The spec timing section and the RTL use 100000 cycles per digit, but an interview answer asks for 131072 cycles (2^17). The RTL and ARCHITECTURE.md use 100000; ARCHITECTURE.md already notes the conflict. The 131072 request was not built.'
- about: press_count_width
  text: 'An interview answer says the press counters are 8-bit and wrap at 256, but spec.yaml registers and the RTL use 32-bit counters wrapping at 2^32. The RTL is what was built.'
- about: segment_order
  text: 'The glyph table in the RTL looks written with segment a on bit 6 (zero is 7''h01), while design.xdc maps seg[0] to CA, segment a. If so, glyphs appear mirrored on the board (a swaps with g, b with f, c with e). This was not checked in simulation against the pins or on hardware.'
- about: reset_values
  text: 'After reset, COUNTER is 0, BRIGHTNESS is 255, CONTROL is 0 (switch brightness off, display enabled), all three press counts are 0, and DESIGN_ID reads 0x54314443 (ASCII T1DC). INPUT_STATUS has no stored state: it always shows live inputs, so its spec reset value of 0 only holds while all inputs are low.'
- about: input_status_raw
  text: 'INPUT_STATUS bits 7:0 are the switches, bit 8 up, bit 9 down, bit 10 centre. They are the raw pin levels captured by one flop in win_rdata, not synchronised or debounced; a read during a bounce can return any level.'
- about: unmapped_access
  text: 'Only offsets 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 and 28 decode, with exact match. A read of any other window offset returns 0. A write to any other offset, or to a read-only register, is ignored, and the shell still returns an OK status, so no error is reported.'
- about: partial_write
  text: 'Writes are always 32 bits; only the low bits are kept (COUNTER 16, BRIGHTNESS 8, CONTROL 2) and the upper bits are dropped without notice. Reads are zero-extended. There are no byte strobes. Reading has no side effects: reads do not clear any counter.'
- about: counter_priority
  text: 'Any window write, to any address including unmapped or read-only ones, suppresses a button update of COUNTER in that cycle, not only a write to COUNTER. Otherwise centre beats up, and up beats down. The three press counters increment independently of this priority, so a suppressed press is still counted.'
- about: control_masking
  text: 'CONTROL bit 1 blanks all digits (an high, segments off) but the scan keeps running and the LEDs are unaffected. CONTROL bit 0 swaps the brightness for both the LED duty and the two brightness digits on AN[7:6]; BRIGHTNESS is not changed.'
- about: pwm_rounding
  text: 'Brightness 0 is always off and 255 always on. Other values turn the LEDs on while pwm_phase is below ceil(brightness x PWM_PERIOD_CYCLES / 255), so the on-time is rounded up rather than exactly linear.'
- about: io_timing
  text: 'design.xdc sets input and output delays and then declares false paths from every input and to every output, so the pin paths are not checked by timing analysis.'
- about: parameter_ranges
  text: 'Assumption: the legal ranges in the parameter table are read from the RTL width and compare logic. Only the default values were exercised by the benches.'

- about: latency_counts
  text: Counted from the RTL, not measured. A button passes two synchroniser flops and the debounce counter; the counter,
    the debounced state and the press count all update on the same clock edge, so the spec's "next sys_clk edge after qualification"
    holds. A software write takes effect on the edge after win_wr. A register read returns its data one cycle after win_rd,
    registered in win_rdata. The PWM comparison and the segment decode are combinational from registers, so a brightness
    or counter change shows at the next phase compare or digit slot.
- about: clk_pin
  text: spec.yaml gives the clk pin as W5; design.xdc, which was built, puts clk on E3 with a 10.00 ns clock. All other
    pins in the spec match the XDC. The XDC governs.
- about: reset_style
  text: spec.yaml says reset releases synchronously and resets all design state. The RTL synchronises the release only for
    the shell; the top-level registers use ~cpu_resetn directly (see resets). design.xdc also marks cpu_resetn as a false
    path, so the reset release is not timed.
- about: display_scan_period
  text: The spec timing section and the RTL use 100000 cycles per digit, but an interview answer asks for 131072 cycles
    (2^17). The RTL and ARCHITECTURE.md use 100000; ARCHITECTURE.md already notes the conflict. The 131072 request was not
    built.
- about: press_count_width
  text: An interview answer says the press counters are 8-bit and wrap at 256, but spec.yaml registers and the RTL use 32-bit
    counters wrapping at 2^32. The RTL is what was built.
- about: segment_order
  text: The glyph table in the RTL looks written with segment a on bit 6 (zero is 7'h01), while design.xdc maps seg[0] to
    CA, segment a. If so, glyphs appear mirrored on the board (a swaps with g, b with f, c with e). This was not checked
    in simulation against the pins or on hardware.
- about: reset_values
  text: 'After reset, COUNTER is 0, BRIGHTNESS is 255, CONTROL is 0 (switch brightness off, display enabled), all three
    press counts are 0, and DESIGN_ID reads 0x54314443 (ASCII T1DC). INPUT_STATUS has no stored state: it always shows live
    inputs, so its spec reset value of 0 only holds while all inputs are low.'
- about: input_status_raw
  text: INPUT_STATUS bits 7:0 are the switches, bit 8 up, bit 9 down, bit 10 centre. They are the raw pin levels captured
    by one flop in win_rdata, not synchronised or debounced; a read during a bounce can return any level.
- about: unmapped_access
  text: Only offsets 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 and 28 decode, with exact match. A read of any other window offset returns
    0. A write to any other offset, or to a read-only register, is ignored, and the shell still returns an OK status, so
    no error is reported.
- about: partial_write
  text: 'Writes are always 32 bits; only the low bits are kept (COUNTER 16, BRIGHTNESS 8, CONTROL 2) and the upper bits
    are dropped without notice. Reads are zero-extended. There are no byte strobes. Reading has no side effects: reads do
    not clear any counter.'
- about: counter_priority
  text: Any window write, to any address including unmapped or read-only ones, suppresses a button update of COUNTER in
    that cycle, not only a write to COUNTER. Otherwise centre beats up, and up beats down. The three press counters increment
    independently of this priority, so a suppressed press is still counted.
- about: control_masking
  text: CONTROL bit 1 blanks all digits (an high, segments off) but the scan keeps running and the LEDs are unaffected.
    CONTROL bit 0 swaps the brightness for both the LED duty and the two brightness digits on AN[7:6]; BRIGHTNESS is not
    changed.
- about: pwm_rounding
  text: Brightness 0 is always off and 255 always on. Other values turn the LEDs on while pwm_phase is below ceil(brightness
    x PWM_PERIOD_CYCLES / 255), so the on-time is rounded up rather than exactly linear.
- about: io_timing
  text: design.xdc sets input and output delays and then declares false paths from every input and to every output, so the
    pin paths are not checked by timing analysis.
- about: parameter_ranges
  text: 'Assumption: the legal ranges in the parameter table are read from the RTL width and compare logic. Only the default
    values were exercised by the benches.'
